readings.title: The Lord's Wrath Unleashed
readings.subtitle: Zion's Splendor Cast Down
readings.text:
[Lamentations 2:1] How <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in <dn>His</dn> displeasure Has covered the daughter of Tsiyon with a cloud! <dn>He</dn> has cast down from the heavens to the earth The comeliness of Yisra’ěl, And has not remembered <dn>His</dn> footstool in the day of <dn>His</dn> displeasure.
[2] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has swallowed up, without compassion, All the pastures of Ya‛aqoḇ. In <dn>His</dn> wrath <dn>He</dn> has thrown down The strongholds of the daughter of Yehuḏah. <dn>He</dn> has brought them down to the ground. <dn>He</dn> has profaned the reign and its rulers.
[3] In the heat of displeasure <dn>He</dn> has cut off every horn of Yisra’ěl. <dn>He</dn> has withdrawn <dn>His</dn> right hand from before the enemy. And <dn>He</dn> burns against Ya‛aqoḇ Like a flaming fire, consuming all around.
[4] <dn>He</dn> has bent <dn>His</dn> bow like an enemy. <dn>He</dn> has set <dn>His</dn> right hand like an adversary. And <dn>He</dn> kills all who delighted the eye. In the tent of the daughter of Tsiyon, <dn>He</dn> has poured out <dn>His</dn> wrath like fire.
[5] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has been like an enemy. <dn>He</dn> has swallowed up Yisra’ěl, <dn>He</dn> has swallowed up all her palaces, <dn>He</dn> has destroyed her strongholds. And <dn>He</dn> increases mourning and lamentation In the daughter of Yehuḏah.
[6] <dn>He</dn> has demolished <dn>His</dn> booth like a garden, <dn>He</dn> has destroyed <dn>His</dn> place of meeting. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made the appointed times and Sabbaths To be forgotten in Tsiyon, And despises sovereign and priest In <dn>His</dn> raging displeasure.
[7] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has cast off <dn>His</dn> slaughter-place, <dn>He</dn> has rejected <dn>His</dn> set-apart place, <dn>He</dn> has delivered the walls of her palaces Into the hand of the enemy. They have made a noise in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> As on the day of an appointed time.
[8] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has planned to destroy The wall of the daughter of Tsiyon. <dn>He</dn> has stretched out a line. <dn>He</dn> has not turned back <dn>His</dn> hand from destroying. And <dn>He</dn> has made the rampart and wall to lament; Together they have languished.
[9] Her gates have sunk into the ground. <dn>He</dn> has destroyed and broken her bars. Her sovereign and her rulers are among the nations. The Torah is no more, And her prophets have found no vision from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The City's Agony
readings.subtitle: Elders Weep and Enemies Mock
readings.text:
[10] The elders of the daughter of Tsiyon Sit on the ground, are silent. They have thrown dust on their heads, They have girded themselves with sackcloth. The maidens of Yerushalayim Have let their heads hang to the ground.
[11] My eyes are spent with tears, My inward parts ferment, My bile has been poured on the ground Because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, As children and the infants languish In the streets of the city.
[12] They say to their mothers, “Where is grain and wine?” As they languish like the wounded In the streets of the city, As their life is poured out in their mothers’ bosom.
[13] How shall I admonish you, To what shall I compare you, O daughter of Yerushalayim? To what shall I liken you to comfort you, O maiden daughter of Tsiyon? For your breach is as great as the sea. Who shall heal you?
[14] Your prophets have seen Falsehood and folly for you, And have not shown you your crookedness, To turn back your captivity. But their visions for you Are false and misleading messages.
[15] All who pass by have clapped their hands at you. They have whistled, And they shake their heads At the daughter of Yerushalayim, “Is this the city that is called ‘The perfection of loveliness, The joy of all the earth’?”
[16] All your enemies have opened Their mouth against you; They have whistled and they gnash their teeth. They say, “We have swallowed her up! This is certainly the day we waited for; We have found it, we have seen it.”
[17] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done what <dn>He</dn> planned, <dn>He</dn> has filled <dn>His</dn> word Which <dn>He</dn> commanded in days of old. <dn>He</dn> has torn down, without compassion, And <dn>He</dn> has let your enemy rejoice over you. <dn>He</dn> has exalted the horn of your adversaries.

readings.title: A Cry from the Walls
readings.subtitle: "See, O YeHoVaH, and Look!"
readings.text:
[18] Their heart cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “O wall of the daughter of Tsiyon, Let tears run down like a river day and night. Give yourself no numbness, Let your eyes have no rest.
[19] “Arise, cry out in the night, At the beginning of the watches, Pour out your heart like water Before the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Lift your hands toward <dn>Him</dn> For the life of your young children, Who languish from hunger At the head of every street.
[20] “See, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and look attentively To whom have <dn>You</dn> done thus. Should the women eat their offspring, Infants of a hand breadth? Should the priest and prophet be killed In the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?
[21] “Young and old lie on the ground in the streets. My maidens and my young men have fallen by the sword. <dn>You</dn> have killed them in the day of <dn>Your</dn> displeasure, <dn>You</dn> have slaughtered without compassion.
[22] “Would <dn>You</dn> proclaim, as in a day of appointed time, The fears that surround me? And no one escaped or survived In the day of the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Those whom <dn>I</dn> have nursed and brought up <dn>My</dn> enemy has destroyed.”

readings.title: The Man Who Has Seen Affliction
readings.subtitle: Under the Rod of His Wrath
readings.text:
[Lamentations 3:1] <dn>I</dn> am the man who has seen affliction By the rod of <dn>His</dn> wrath.
[2] <dn>He</dn> has led me and made me walk In darkness and not light.
[3] Indeed, <dn>He</dn> has turned back, <dn>He</dn> has turned <dn>His</dn> hand against me all the day.
[4] <dn>He</dn> has worn out my flesh and my skin, <dn>He</dn> has broken my bones.
[5] <dn>He</dn> has piled up against me, And surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
[6] <dn>He</dn> has made me dwell in dark places Like the dead of old.
[7] <dn>He</dn> has hedged me in and <dn>I</dn> do not go out, <dn>He</dn> has made my chain heavy.
[8] Also, when <dn>I</dn> cry and shout, <dn>He</dn> shuts out my prayer.
[9] <dn>He</dn> has blocked my ways with hewn stone, <dn>He</dn> has made my paths crooked.
[10] <dn>He</dn> is to me like a bear lying in wait, A lion in hiding.
[11] <dn>He</dn> has turned aside my ways And torn me in pieces, <dn>He</dn> has laid me waste.
[12] <dn>He</dn> has bent <dn>His</dn> bow And set me up as a target for the arrow.
[13] <dn>He</dn> made the arrows of <dn>His</dn> quiver pierce my kidneys.
[14] <dn>I</dn> have been a mockery to all my people, Their mocking song all the day.
[15] <dn>He</dn> has filled me with bitterness, <dn>He</dn> drenched me with wormwood.
[16] And <dn>He</dn> has broken my teeth with gravel, <dn>He</dn> has covered me with ashes.
[17] And <dn>You</dn> have removed my being far from peace, <dn>I</dn> have forgotten goodness.
[18] And <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>My</dn> strength and <dn>my</dn> expectancy Have perished from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”

readings.title: A Turn to Hope
readings.subtitle: His Loving-Commitments Never End
readings.text:
[19] Remember my affliction and my anguish, The wormwood and the gall.
[20] <dn>Your</dn> being indeed remembers And bows down upon me.
[21] This <dn>I</dn> recall to my mind, therefore <dn>I</dn> wait:
[22] The loving-commitments of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! For we have not been consumed, For <dn>His</dn> compassions have not ended.
[23] They are new every morning, Great is <dn>Your</dn> trustworthiness.
[24] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is my Portion,” says my being, “Therefore <dn>I</dn> wait for <dn>Him</dn>!”
[25] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is good to those waiting for <dn>Him</dn>, To the being who seeks <dn>Him</dn>.
[26] It is good – both to wait and to be silent, For the deliverance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[27] It is good for a man to bear a yoke in his youth.
[28] Let him sit alone and be silent, Because <dn>He</dn> has laid it on him.
[29] Let him put his mouth in the dust, There might yet be expectancy.
[30] Let him give his cheek To the one who strikes him – <dn>He</dn> is filled with reproach.
[31] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not cast off forever.
[32] For though <dn>He</dn> afflicted, Yet <dn>He</dn> shall show compassion According to the greatness of <dn>His</dn> loving-commitments.
[33] For <dn>He</dn> has not afflicted from <dn>His</dn> heart, Nor does <dn>He</dn> grieve the children of men.
[34] To crush under <dn>His</dn> feet All the prisoners of the earth,
[35] To turn aside the right-ruling of man Before the face of the Most High,
[36] Or wrong a man in his cause – This <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not approve.
[37] Who was it that spoke, And it came to be! Has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> not commanded it?
[38] Do not the evils and the good Come out of the mouth of the Most High?
[39] What? Should mankind complain, A living man, because of his sins?

readings.title: A Call to Repentance
readings.subtitle: "We Have Transgressed and Rebelled"
readings.text:
[40] Let us search and examine our ways, And turn back to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[41] Let us lift our hearts and hands To <dn>Ěl</dn> in the heavens and say:
[42] <dn>We</dn>, we have transgressed and rebelled. <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have not forgiven.
[43] <dn>You</dn> have wrapped <dn>Yourself</dn> With displeasure and pursued us. <dn>You</dn> have killed, <dn>You</dn> have not shown compassion.
[44] <dn>You</dn> have wrapped <dn>Yourself</dn> With a cloud, so that prayer does not pass through.
[45] <dn>You</dn> make us as scum and refuse In the midst of the peoples.
[46] All our enemies have opened their mouth against us.
[47] Fear and a snare have come upon us, Shame and ruin.
[48] Streams of water run down my eye For the ruin of the daughter of my people.
[49] <dn>My</dn> eye flows out and does not cease, Without stopping,
[50] Until <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looks down and sees from the heavens.
[51] <dn>My</dn> eye pains my being Because of all the daughters of my city.
[52] <dn>My</dn> enemies hunted me down Like a bird, without cause.
[53] They have cut off my life in the pit, And they threw stones at me.
[54] Waters flowed over my head; <dn>I</dn> said, “<dn>I</dn> am cut off!”

readings.title: A Plea from the Pit
readings.subtitle: "You Have Redeemed My Life"
readings.text:
[55] <dn>I</dn> called on <dn>Your</dn> Name, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, from the lowest pit.
[56] <dn>You</dn> have heard my voice, Do not hide <dn>Your</dn> ear from my groaning, From my outcry!
[57] <dn>You</dn> drew near on the day <dn>I</dn> called on <dn>You</dn>; <dn>You</dn> said, <dq>“Do not fear!”</dq>
[58] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> did plead the case for my being; <dn>You</dn> have redeemed my life.
[59] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have seen my oppression; Judge my case.
[60] <dn>You</dn> have seen <dn>את</dn> all their vengeance, All their plans against me.
[61] <dn>You</dn> have heard their reproach, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all their plans against me,
[62] The lips of those rising against me, And their scheming against me all the day.
[63] Look at their sitting down and their rising up; <dn>I</dn> am their song.
[64] Repay them, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, According to the work of their hands.
[65] Give them a veiled heart, <dn>Your</dn> curse upon them!
[66] Pursue and destroy them in displeasure, From under the heavens of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Horrors of the Siege
readings.subtitle: Gold Dimmed, Children Starving
readings.text:
[Lamentations 4:1] How dim the gold has become, The fine gold changed! The stones of the set-apart place Are scattered at the head of every street.
[2] The precious sons of Tsiyon Who were weighed against fine gold, How they have been reckoned as clay pots, The work of the hands of the potter!
[3] Even jackals have presented their breasts, They have nursed their young. The daughter of my people has become as cruel, As ostriches in the wilderness.
[4] The tongue of the infant has clung To the roof of its mouth for thirst; Children asked for bread, No one breaks it for them.
[5] Those who ate delicacies Have been laid waste in the streets; Those who were brought up in scarlet Have embraced dunghills.
[6] And the crookedness of the daughter of my people Is greater than the punishment of the sin of Seḏom, Which was overthrown in a moment, And no hands were wrung over her!
[7] Her Nazirites were brighter than snow And whiter than milk; More ruddy in body than rubies, Their cut like sapphire.
[8] Their appearance has become blacker than soot; They have become unrecognised in the streets; Their skin has shrivelled on their bones, It has become dry, it has become as wood.
[9] Better off were those pierced by the sword Than those pierced by hunger; For these pine away, Pierced through for lack of the fruits of the field.
[10] The hands of the compassionate women Have boiled their own children; They became food for them In the destruction of the daughter of my people.
[11] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has completed <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> wrath, <dn>He</dn> has poured out <dn>His</dn> burning displeasure. And <dn>He</dn> kindled a fire in Tsiyon, And it consumed her foundations.

readings.title: The Cause and the Consequence
readings.subtitle: Zion's Iniquity Completed, Edom's Judged
readings.text:
[12] The sovereigns of the earth did not believe, Nor any of the inhabitants of the world, That an adversary and enemy Would enter the gates of Yerushalayim.
[13] It was because of the sins of her prophets, The crookednesses of her priests, Who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
[14] They staggered, blind, in the streets; They have defiled themselves with blood, So that no one was able to touch their garments.
[15] They shouted at them, “Away! Unclean! Away! Away! Touch not!” When they fled and staggered, They said, among the nations, “They shall stay no longer.”
[16] The face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> scattered them. <dn>He</dn> no longer regards them. They showed no respect for the priests Nor favour to the elders.
[17] While we exist, our eyes are consumed, Watching vainly for our help. In our watch-tower we watched for a nation That could not save.
[18] They have hunted our steps From going in our streets. Our end was near, Our days were completed, For our end had come.
[19] Our pursuers were swifter Than the eagles of the heavens. They came hotly after us on the mountains And lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
[20] The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Was caught in their pits, In whose shadow we had thought To live among the nations.
[21] Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Eḏom, <dn>You</dn> who dwell in the land of Uz! The cup is to pass over to you too, So that you become drunk and make yourself naked.
[22] <dn>Your</dn> crookedness has been completed, O daughter of Tsiyon. <dn>He</dn> no longer prolongs your exile. <dn>He</dn> shall punish your crookedness, O daughter of Eḏom, <dn>He</dn> shall uncover your sins!
